A recently translated interview with Miyamoto from twenty years ago discussing the development of Yoshi's Island.

I never would have guessed that was a 5 year project. They spent 2 years just experimenting with different concepts...this is why Nintendo is a fantastic game producer. Most AAA console games these days are around 12-24 month development cycles, and it really shows in how rushed they truly are.

You get the occasional gem like the first Assassin's Creed or Red Dead where they spend 4 years on a crazy project and it really pays off. If either of those games had a normal dev cycle they would have flopped for sure. They luckily were made in studios that were their own publisherspublishers, which makes a night and day difference in the game industry.

Mario games always have a massive amount of work and polish put into them. Each Mario game is a classic in its own right (at least the main titles.) This is why I love Nintendo so much. Every game feels like a labor of love.

Having grown up with Yoshi's Island and Super Mario as a kid, it still amazes me how the engineers and coders at Nintendo managed to pull games like this out of the SNES's seemingly archaic hardware (from a modern perspective, that is).
